# Webhooks and callbacks

Akoro receives provider-signed webhooks for payments. Webhooks are authenticated
by the provider's signature, not by a user session.

## Payment webhooks

Payments are processed by Paystack. Akoro verifies the webhook signature once
against the raw request body.

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/webhooks/paystack` | Unified Paystack webhook |
| `POST /api/payments/verify` | Legacy Paystack verification |
| `POST /api/payouts/webhook` | Payout / transfer status |

## Signature verification

The `x-paystack-signature` header carries an HMAC-SHA512 digest of the exact
request body. Requests with an invalid signature are rejected with `400`.

Because the signature is computed over the raw body, send the body unmodified —
do not re-encode or reformat it.

## Reliability

- Events are recorded before processing so a failed attempt is auditable.
- Writes use an outbox with idempotency keys; a redelivered event is applied once.
- Respond `2xx` quickly so the provider does not retry an already-processed
  event.

## Consuming webhooks

Webhooks are inbound only. If you build your own integration that mirrors these
callbacks, verify the signature the same way and keep consumers idempotent.
